title: Precision-based eval thresholds & staged apply for batch/cache autotuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We're building a precision-first evaluation and staged-apply workflow for automated batching/caching recommendations. The autotuner currently suggests config changes that materially reduce token costs but occasionally cause subtle quality regressions for certain workloads (structured responses, code, multi-turn contexts). This ticket defines the evaluation signals, calibrated thresholds, rollout gating, and automatic rollback criteria to safely apply autotune recommendations at scale.

Goals: 1) Define ensemble metrics that reliably surface regressions relevant to product behavior (not just token-level differences). 2) Calibrate per-model and per-workload acceptance thresholds using historical A/B data. 3) Implement a four-stage apply pipeline (dry-run -> shadow -> canary -> ramp) with automated gating and rollback. 4) Add CI/PR blocking checks and runtime hooks to enforce safety.

Scope (what we will deliver in this ticket):
- Eval harness extension that computes: embedding cosine similarity (OpenAI-compatible embeddings), structural field match rate (for JSON/structured outputs), context-aware token divergence (weighted by position), and generation-level quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE adapted for open-ended outputs).
- Threshold calibration job that produces baseline distributions per-model and workload and writes final thresholds to config-store.
- Staged apply orchestration that integrates with Autotune Controller: dry-run (no traffic), shadow (mirror traffic), canary (1-5% traffic), ramp (gradual to 100% if all gates pass).
- Automatic rollback actions and incident playbook entries for human-in-the-loop escalation.

Non-goals: tuning kernel selection or batching internals (handled in separate runtime tickets), large-scale rework of the Console UI (we will emit events/hooks for Console to consume).

Why a precision-first approach: Prior rollouts showed that naive token-divergence triggers either miss semantic shifts or over-trigger on benign phrasing. Combining semantic similarity with structural checks reduces false positives for regressions that matter to end-users (e.g., missing JSON keys, incorrect code snippets, or hallucinated facts).

High-level acceptance flow: recommended config -> dry-run eval on replayed request trace -> compute metrics and compare to calibrated thresholds -> if pass, create shadow deploy and run live sentinel traffic for X hours -> collect metrics and SLA signals -> if thresholds still pass, open canary rollout -> monitor for at least N requests and user-facing error rate delta -> auto-ramp if green or rollback if any critical gate trips.
acceptance_criteria: Eval harness produces embedding cosine + structural match + position-weighted token divergence for any model in our catalog
Threshold calibration job generates per-model, per-workload thresholds and stores them in config-store with versioned metadata
Dry-run replay returns evaluation report (pass/fail) within 15 minutes for typical 10k-sample replay
Shadow stage runs for configurable window and emits metrics to cost-safety dashboard and anomaly detector
Canary stage can be automatically promoted or rolled back based on gates within 2 hours without manual intervention
Automatic rollback reverts runtime config and pins last-known-good config; an incident ticket is auto-created when rollback occurs
tasks: Design evaluation metric spec and schema (embedding + structural + token-divergence)
Implement evaluation runner library and integrate with existing eval infra
Build threshold calibration job (historical A/B analysis, 95th/5th percentile decisions)
Add staged apply states to Autotune Controller and wire gating checks
Create CI gating that runs eval harness on PRs touching autotune rules
Add dashboard panels and alerts for regression signals and auto-rollback events
Write runbook and SLA for incident handling and manual rollback flow
End-to-end integration tests using synthetic workloads and replay traces
notes: 2026-03-01: Kickoff with PM/Product (Daniel Ruiz) and SRE (Priya Kapoor). Agreed to prioritize semantically meaningful signals over raw token deltas.

2026-03-03: Prototype eval runner (branch: feat/autotune-eval-runner) — PR at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2741. Early results on internal trace show embedding cosine is most predictive for open-ended chat loss of meaning.

2026-03-06: Decision: use anchor prompt set (50 representative prompts per workload) instead of 'golden prompt' nomenclature to reduce bias in selection. Anchor set will be curated by PM + Solutions Eng.

2026-03-08: Trade-off: stricter structural-match thresholds catch more regressions for structured outputs but reduce number of safe applies by ~18% in baseline simulation. We accepted a slightly looser threshold for batch-cache changes and stricter for cache-key semantics due to higher risk on stateful sessions.
2026-03-10: Integrated shadow routing prototype emits metrics to Cost-Safety dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/cost-safety/autotune/38820 (internal).
2026-03-12: Implemented automatic rollback action that pins previous config and annotates config-store with rollback reason; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autotune-controller/pull/89
2026-03-14: Running calibration job across production traces for llama-3-70b and wheels-13b. Initial thresholds drafted and uploaded to GCS: gs://redwood-evals/38820/thresholds-v0.json
